paper.title: Addressing the weight of the issue: gaps in obesity education among US osteopathic medical students.
paper.summary:
CONTEXT: Obesity is a significant public health concern, with the United States experiencing some of the highest obesity rates worldwide. Despite the widespread prevalence and negative impacts on patient health, obesity education in medical school curricula remains insufficient. This training deficit contributes to a lack of preparedness among medical students in the management of obesity, leading to healthcare provider bias and inadequate patient care.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to identify potential gaps in obesity education within US osteopathic medical schools by assessing current osteopathic medical students' knowledge, confidence, and perceptions of medical school obesity education.
METHODS: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was distributed to osteopathic medical students across all 42 US osteopathic medical schools through the Student Osteopathic Medical Association (SOMA) weekly emails, SOMA internal chapter emails, and SOMA social media accounts from October 2024 to December 2024. The inclusion criteria were that participants had to be currently enrolled first-, second-, third-, and fourth-year osteopathic medical students and provide informed consent. The responses were summarized utilizing descriptive analysis. Each survey question was analyzed independently, considering the varying number of responses received per question.
RESULTS: A total of 208 students participated in the survey. Out of the 208 respondents, most students felt somewhat prepared (38.5 %) or unprepared/very unprepared (32.7 %) to manage obesity and provide nutrition education in the clinical setting. Due to the number of participants, the responses are considered in aggregate and not grouped by cohort year. In addition, there was nearly an even split among students regarding comfort in discussing obesity and weight management with patients, with 30.6 % stating that they are uncomfortable or very uncomfortable, 37.4 % reporting being somewhat comfortable, and 32.0 % feeling comfortable or very comfortable. Only 14.1 % of students reported having standardized patient encounters regarding obesity counseling, with most of these encounters (55.2 %) lasting less than 30 min. Regarding comfort discussing weight bias and stigma, 59.8 % of the students reported feeling somewhat comfortable, comfortable, or very comfortable discussing weight bias and stigma, while 40.2 % were slightly uncomfortable or not comfortable addressing the topic with patients. Given the limited sample size and response rate, these findings are exploratory and limited by a low response rate and potential response bias.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest potential gaps in obesity education among the responding osteopathic medical students. While limited by sample size and possible response bias, the results highlight opportunities for strengthening obesity-related curricula, particularly in experiential learning and weight bias training.

paper.title: Nanofat Transfer to the Face: How We Do It.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: Nanofat transfer is a mechanically emulsified, cell-based autologous fat product used to improve facial skin quality through the paracrine activity of adipose-derived stem cells and growth factors.
OBJECTIVE: To provide dermatologic surgeons with a practical, step-by-step review of nanofat harvesting, processing, emulsification, and delivery technique for facial rejuvenation, along with a summary of the supporting clinical evidence and safety profile.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This review describes established supplies, donor-site harvesting technique, washing and purification options (gravity decantation, cotton gauze rolling, centrifugation, and closed washing/filtration systems), mechanical emulsification, and dermal delivery technique, synthesized from the published nanofat literature.
RESULTS: Across the reviewed literature, nanofat improves dermal thickness, collagen density, hydration, and fine rhytides, with an established role in scar treatment and emerging applications in androgenetic alopecia, wound healing, and pigmentary conditions. Reported adverse events are mild and self-limited, and the technique carries a favorable overall safety profile.
CONCLUSION: Nanofat transfer is a simple, in-office, autologous technique that offers dermatologic surgeons a versatile option for facial skin rejuvenation when attention is paid to gentle harvesting, appropriate processing, thorough emulsification, and precise delivery.

paper.title: Mindful Awareness as a Mediator Between Social Appearance Anxiety and Social Media Addiction in Adolescents.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: Adolescence is a critical period for identity formation and social development, and social media can shape appearance perceptions and social acceptance. Social appearance anxiety may be associated with greater vulnerability to social media addiction, whereas mindful awareness may be linked to lower levels of this risk. The current study tested mindful awareness as a mediator between social appearance anxiety and social media addiction in adolescents.
METHOD: The sample comprised 383 volunteer secondary school students in eastern Türkiye during the 2024-2025 academic year. Participants completed standardized measures of social appearance anxiety, mindful awareness, and social media addiction.
RESULTS: Social appearance anxiety was positively related to social media addiction and negatively related to mindful awareness; mindful awareness was also negatively related to addiction.
CONCLUSION: Mediation results indicated partial mediation, suggesting mindfulness-based interventions may reduce appearance anxiety and promote healthier social media use among adolescents. Findings highlight mindful awareness as a target for prevention.

paper.title: The Impact of Problematic Online Gambling on University Students' Lives: Exploring Links With Impulsivity, Emotion Regulation, and Psychological Distress.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: To examine the effect of problematic online gambling on the lives of university students in the context of impulsivity, emotion regulation, and psychological distress.
METHOD: This descriptive and correlational study was conducted with 200 university students who engage in online gambling. Data were collected using the Online Gambling Addiction Scale, Barratt Impulsivity Scale, Emotion Regulation Difficulties Scale, and Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21.
RESULTS: Of students, 93.5% were found to exhibit problematic online gambling, 79% lost money, 34.5% reported impaired relationships, 33.5% reported a negative influence on their academic and social activities, and 19% gambled online by stealing or borrowing money. Higher levels of impulsivity, emotion regulation difficulties, depression, anxiety, and stress were associated with higher levels of problematic online gambling (p < .001). These predictor variables explained 19.7% of the variance in problematic online gambling.
CONCLUSION: Current findings may help nurses in developing psychosocial interventions to prevent problematic online gambling in university students.

paper.title: Cancer Screening and Follow Up Among Individuals With Serious Mental Illness.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States. Individuals with serious mental illness (SMI) have higher cancer mortality, which may be due to lower screening rates and barriers to timely, effective care. The current study explored how individuals with SMI perceive cancer screening and follow up to identify barriers and facilitators to care.
METHOD: Using a qualitative interpretive description approach, we conducted individual interviews with 10 adults with SMI about their cancer screening experiences.
RESULTS: The most frequently reported barriers were distrust of the health care system, psychiatric symptoms, fear, low prioritization, and shame. Facilitators included support systems, regular primary care, positive health care experiences, and personal agency.
CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the importance of providing supportive health care services and strengthening personal agency as key components of recovery and cancer screening and follow up in individuals with SMI.

paper.title: Influence of Trained Companion Dog Ownership Among Military Veterans Diagnosed With a Mental Health Condition.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: To explore the perceptions of U.S. Veterans on the influence of owning trained companion dogs (TCDs) from animal shelters on their mental health and influence of the historical distress of the dog on dog-owner bonding.
METHOD: A descriptive, exploratory design was used to collect data via telephone interviews with 90 veterans who adopted dogs and had a mental health diagnosis at the time of adoption.
RESULTS: Ownership influenced perceptions of loneliness (97%), sense of purpose (87%), exercise (86%), safety (86%), anxiety (84%), depression (84%), and sleep (74%). Veterans who perceived that their dog experienced distress or trauma pre-adoption acknowledged it influenced feelings of connectedness (66%), relating to the dog (81%), helping the dog (81%), and the dog helping them (88%).
CONCLUSION: TCD ownership positively influenced veteran mental health. Help is a two-way street between veterans and dogs with a history of distress or trauma. Health care professionals caring for veterans with mental health conditions should explore dog ownership through specific companion programs.

paper.title: Effectiveness of a Humor-Integrated Cognitive-Behavioral Psychoeducation Program for Depression: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a humor-integrated cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)-based psychoeducation program in reducing depressive symptoms and improving self-esteem, sense of humor, and adaptive coping in outpatients diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD).
METHOD: Sixty outpatients with MDD were randomized to an experimental group (n = 30) receiving an eight-session nurse-delivered program or a control group (n = 30) receiving standard psychiatric care. Assessments were conducted at baseline, postintervention, and 1- and 3-month follow up.
RESULTS: The experimental group demonstrated significant improvements in all outcomes (p < .05), with large effect sizes for humor measures (Multidimensional Sense of Humor Scale: η2 = 0.572, d = 2.31; Coping Humor Scale: η2 = 0.665, d = 2.82) and moderate-to-large effects for depression (Beck Depression Inventory: η2 = 0.400, d = 1.63) and self-esteem (Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale: η2 = 0.119, d = 0.74), all maintained at follow up.
CONCLUSION: A humor-integrated CBT-based psychoeducation program delivered by specialist psychiatric nurses effectively reduced depressive symptoms and improved adaptive coping among outpatients with MDD.

paper.title: Cracking and Self-Healing in a Molecular Crystal Driven by Topochemical Polymerization.
paper.summary: Topochemical reactions in molecular crystals are often accompanied by severe lattice strain, frequently leading to crystal fracture and loss of crystallinity. Here we report an unusual case in which heat-driven topochemical azide-alkyne cycloaddition (TAAC) polymerization in a non-centrosymmetric molecular crystal induces macroscopic cracking that is followed by autonomous self-healing. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals a regiospecific single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation to a helical polymer, despite large-amplitude molecular motion and anisotropic lattice deformation (a +19.9%, b -2.9%, c -13.3%). Face-indexing and morphology analysis correlate the crystallographic axes with macroscopic crystal dimensions, rationalizing the observed breadth expansion, length contraction, and cleavage along a weakly bound crystallographic plane. Mechanistically, crack formation originates from reaction-induced bimorphic lattice strain, while self-healing is driven by electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged fracture surfaces in the polar crystal, followed by continued intradomain polymerization that eliminates the bimorphic interface. Autonomous healing occurs upon completion of the topochemical polymerization in the crystalline material.
